subject.title: [Feature]:Support per-agent command lanes for multi-agent deployments

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class per-agent foreground command-lane config surface, and if so should it be expressed as explicit lane names, per-agent max concurrency, or a narrower scheduler policy?
rationale: Current code confirms the lower-level lane queue can support named lanes, but adding an agent config/default surface changes scheduler semantics and upgrade behavior, and prior PRs were closed because this needs owner-backed design direction.

options.title: Design explicit per-agent lanes
options.body: Add an opt-in per-agent/default lane config with schema, docs, doctor/validation, and tests while preserving the shared `main` default.

options.title: Use per-agent concurrency only
options.body: Expose a narrower per-agent cap without arbitrary lane names, reducing config surface but leaving some isolation scenarios unsolved.

options.title: Defer to broader orchestration work
options.body: Keep the issue open but block implementation until the adjacent per-channel, browser, and multi-agent orchestration scheduler decisions are resolved together.

recommendation.title: Design explicit per-agent lanes
recommendation.body: Add an opt-in per-agent/default lane config with schema, docs, doctor/validation, and tests while preserving the shared `main` default.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent lane/default/concurrency history and current blamed scheduler surfaces point to steipete as the best available owner for the product-direction choice.
